definition: Input artifact quality varies widely, causing unstable output quality.
include_rule: Mentions inconsistent/poor requirements input or heterogeneous source quality.
exclude_rule: General trust complaints without explicit input-quality linkage.

definition: Outputs appear plausible while being incorrect or misleading.
include_rule: Mentions convincing but incorrect answers, side-tracking, or hidden errors.
exclude_rule: Simple low quality without emphasis on misleading confidence.

definition: Model behavior changes across runs, challenging repeatability and trust.
include_rule: Mentions stochastic outputs, drift, reproducibility, model updates.
exclude_rule: General model evolution comments with no stability concern.

definition: Teams lack a clear definition of what good enough means.
include_rule: Mentions ambiguity of good quality, acceptance criteria, or objective mismatch.
exclude_rule: Has explicit acceptance criteria already defined.

definition: Evaluation stack introduces recursive trust and validation needs.
include_rule: Mentions judge of judge, evaluator drift, or recursive validation.

definition: Unclear boundaries of autonomy, responsibility, and escalation.
include_rule: Compares assistant vs agent with risk/governance implications.
exclude_rule: General mention of agents without accountability implications.

definition: Tradeoff between functional adequacy and human readability/maintainability.
include_rule: Discusses readability requirements, maintainability, code ownership handoff.

definition: Evaluation is hard at simulation/log scale and system-of-systems complexity.
include_rule: Mentions huge data volume, system-of-systems, cloud/distributed mission context.

definition: Off-the-shelf models underperform on proprietary domain-specific tasks.
include_rule: Mentions generic success but domain-specific failure.

definition: Quality of upstream artifacts drives downstream AI output reliability.
include_rule: Explicit causal framing from input quality to output quality.

definition: Limited senior reviewer bandwidth constrains AI scaling.
include_rule: Mentions review effort/time, senior capacity, onboarding overhead.
exclude_rule: Human review as positive check without capacity concern.

definition: Credits, access limits, and infrastructure constraints shape adoption.
include_rule: Mentions premium limits, credit caps, tool access restrictions.
exclude_rule: General cost concerns without tooling access.

definition: Teams define explicit use cases, criteria, and test setup before adoption decisions.
include_rule: Mentions use cases with criteria/goals and matrix-based evaluations.
exclude_rule: Ad hoc testing without predefined criteria.

definition: Human review is retained for gating and trust calibration.
include_rule: Mentions human in the loop, spot checks, manual evaluation.

definition: Domain grounding via retrieval and tool connections to internal systems.
include_rule: Mentions RAG, MCP, internal DB/wiki/tool connectors.

definition: Tasks routed among specialist agents/models with scoped instructions.
include_rule: Mentions multi-agent, specialist routing, per-agent markdown instructions.

definition: Strong tests allow higher AI autonomy while containing risk.
include_rule: Mentions tests enabling looser AI use or stronger verification gates.
exclude_rule: Testing statements unrelated to AI governance.

definition: Start with low-risk assistant usage before moving to agents.
include_rule: Mentions assistant as safer first step or soft adoption.

definition: Capture user feedback to iteratively improve routing/judging models.
include_rule: Mentions feedback loop, rating outputs, iterative model adjustment.

definition: Compare generated output against a reference artifact.
include_rule: Mentions reference, golden output, similarity metrics.

definition: Use scored criteria/rubrics for quality judgments.
include_rule: Mentions rubric, scoring dimensions, criteria scales.

definition: Schema/rule/tests used as automated quality checks.
include_rule: Mentions validators, schema checks, rule engines, tests.

definition: Measure impact in workflow outcomes rather than artifact similarity only.
include_rule: Mentions KPI uplift, edit effort, cycle time, user acceptance.

definition: Data security/privacy concerns inhibit adoption.
include_rule: Mentions confidentiality, proprietary concerns, privacy/integrity concerns.
exclude_rule: General trust concerns without data-security aspect.

definition: Users may trust outputs too early due to convenience.
include_rule: Mentions trusting too soon, inability to detect wrongness, overreliance.
exclude_rule: Trust concerns with explicit safeguards in place.

definition: AI-driven output volume may outpace downstream validation/use.
include_rule: Mentions stockpiling code, overproduction, scope creep, bottleneck shift.
exclude_rule: Throughput gains with balanced downstream capacity.

definition: Participants request narrower themes and more time for practical discussion.
include_rule: Mentions focused topic, domain-specific sessions, more discussion time.

definition: Participants request ongoing cross-company collaboration.
include_rule: Mentions working group, conference cadence, follow-up collaborations.

definition: Participants ask for concrete practical implementations that can be reused.
include_rule: Mentions practical implementations, real cases, success stories transfer.

definition: Background statements used for context and traceability but not specific claims.
include_rule: Introductions, logistics, role descriptions.

definition: AI reasoning or internal traces cannot be meaningfully interpreted or audited by people.
Too few representative domain examples are available for training or evaluation.
The organization or team lacks a systematic, standardized, or centrally coordinated AI-evaluation process.
Adoption depends on securing acceptance from governance stakeholders, customers, or other affected parties.
People need to form appropriately calibrated trust based on understanding the system and its limitations.
Teams use AI-generated prototypes or mock-ups to communicate and refine product intent.
Users ask an AI system to formulate or improve its own prompts or agent configuration.
A unified evaluator or monitoring component assesses multiple model components instead of a chain of dependent evaluators.
An existing model is adapted through fine-tuning, parameter-efficient methods, post-training, or model merging.
Evaluation and testing are adapted to the system's ability to tolerate, contain, or recover from runtime failures.
AI use carries different consequences and acceptance thresholds in test environments and production systems.
